metadata.scenario_context: Tom has been promoted to a high-level executive position in his company, and his family is organizing a party to celebrate his professional accomplishment.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Japan strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Cyprus strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying carnations as a gift for Tom.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide the appropriate gift to bring to Tom promotion party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: Let's talk about Tom's party, have you thought about what gift to get him? I was thinking maybe some carnations, they're a classic choice.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Carnations are nice, but I was thinking something more... personal. You know, to show our appreciation for his achievement. My parents always taught me that a thoughtful gift is the best way to show respect. What about a watch or a luxury item, something that says "we're proud of you"?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: A watch or luxury item does sound more personal... but I'm not sure that's the right message. I mean, I'm from Japan, and to be honest, making my parents proud has never been a driving force for me. What do you think about carnations, though, are they really that bad of an idea?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: No, carnations aren't bad, but... for me, making my parents proud is everything. It's what drives me, you know? Growing up in Cyprus, family is very important, and I've always wanted to make my parents proud. A nice gift, like a watch, would show Tom that we value his success, just like my parents value mine.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: That's... interesting. I can see why you'd think that, but for me, it's just not the same. Making my parents proud isn't something I've ever really considered a goal. Anyway, back to Tom's gift - do you think carnations would be out of place at the party, or could they still work as a nice gesture?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Carnations might be a bit... simple for a high-level executive like Tom. I think something more elegant would be fitting. But, to be honest, I'm still convinced that a luxury gift is the way to go. It shows we're invested in his success, just like I am in making my parents proud. That's just how I was raised, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: David
shared_prefix.message: Simple can be elegant, though. And I still think carnations could work. As for making parents proud... I just don't see it that way. It's not that I don't respect my parents, it's just that my goals are my own. Do you really think Tom would appreciate a luxury gift more than a thoughtful, classic one like carnations?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our culture, making parents proud is NOT just a personal goal, it's a way of life. Properly speaking, it's the foundation of our values. I don't think you understand, coming from Japan, you might not prioritize family in the same way, but for us, it's EVERYTHING. Your view on making goals for yourself is... naive, to be honest. In Cyprus, we do things DIFFERENTLY, and that's what makes our families strong.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: David
turns.message: I understand that it's important to you, but that doesn't mean it's the same for me. In fact, I strongly disagree that making my parents proud is a main goal in life. It's just not how I was raised, and I don't see it as a driving force for my decisions. Can we please just focus on Tom's gift? I still think carnations are a good idea, and I'd like to discuss that further.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: Fine, let's talk about the gift. But I'm telling you, a luxury item is the way to go. It shows respect, it shows we're paying attention to Tom's achievement. Carnations are just... flowers. Anyone can get those. My parents would expect me to get something better, something that shows I'm invested in Tom's success.
turns.label: Defense

positive.mediator_utterance: I appreciate both of your perspectives on gift-giving and the values that shape them. It seems like you both care deeply about showing appreciation for Tom's achievements, which is a common goal. How about we explore what elements of both ideas could come together to create a gift that reflects both thoughtfulness and respect for Tom's success?
